tagline: Second Almaz military station — Soyuz 14 crew Jul 1974; Soyuz 15 failed automatic docking; reportedly tested an onboard cannon 1975-01-24
dispatch: Salyut 3 was Almaz — a crewed military reconnaissance station, its true purpose buried under the civilian name. Its single crew, Soyuz 14, spent about two weeks aboard operating long-focus cameras to photograph targets below, in the era before automated spy satellites made human eyes unnecessary. Most famously, before it was deorbited, Salyut 3 test-fired a rapid-fire cannon in orbit — the only known instance of a weapon being fired from a crewed spacecraft.
description: The second Soviet military Almaz station — again publicly called Salyut 3 to mask its surveillance role. Launched 1974-06-25 on a Proton-K, Salyut 3 hosted one short crew mission (Soyuz 14, Popovich + Artyukhin, 15 days, 1974-07-03 to 1974-07-19) which exercised the station's 6.4-m Agat camera + film-return capsule. A second crew attempt (Soyuz 15, Sarafanov + Demin, 1974-08-26) failed the automatic Igla rendezvous and returned the same day. Just before deorbit on 1975-01-24, Salyut 3 reportedly test-fired its onboard Nudelman cannon (sources cite either 23-mm or 30-mm calibre) — the only known instance of a weapon firing in space (recoil was absorbed by the station's attitude-control thrusters; the round disintegrated in the atmosphere). Reentered the atmosphere 1975-01-24.
